_meta.purpose: Patient <-> trial labels for evaluating retrieval ranking and scoring accuracy.

schema.rationale: one sentence citing the deciding eligibility criterion

_meta.status: CRITERIA-DERIVED (annotator=criteria-derived-v1), NOT clinician-reviewed. Each (patient, trial) pair was labeled by reading the trial's actual ClinicalTrials.gov eligibility criteria and applying deterministic rules: tumor type, biomarker/receptor state, disease stage, prior-therapy exclusions, and demographic bounds. MATCH = clearly eligible on documented criteria; PARTIAL = eligible pending undocumented data or borderline on a secondary criterion (e.g. ECOG off by one, unconfirmed mutation codon); NO = a documented criterion clearly disqualifies. Judgment calls needing true oncology expertise were labeled PARTIAL rather than guessed. Replace with clinician review before using these numbers for any clinical claim.

coverage.note: Labels cover trials that the retriever actually surfaced for these 8 patients (harvested 2026-07-10). Because relevant trials were drawn from the retrieved set, retrieval recall@k is bounded by construction (near 1.0) and MRR is the more informative retrieval signal here; the scoring confusion matrix is the primary, well-posed metric. A recall study over independently-sourced eligible trials is the honest next step.

labeling_protocol: 1. python -m eval.run_eval --dump-trials <N> lists trials currently retrieved.
2. Read each trial's eligibility criteria (fetched from ClinicalTrials.gov) against the patient profile.
3. Assign MATCH / PARTIAL / NO per the definitions in _meta.status, citing the deciding criterion.
4. For a real recall study, add independently-sourced known-eligible NCT ids (may be outside current retrieval).
5. For clinical use, have an oncologist review and overwrite annotator with their id.
